Article.ArticleTitle: A direct role for hepatitis B virus X protein in inducing mitochondrial membrane permeabilization.

Abstract.AbstractText: Hepatitis B virus X protein (HBx) acts as a multifunctional protein that regulates intracellular signaling pathways during HBV infection. It has mainly been studied in terms of its interaction with cellular proteins. Here, we show that HBx induces membrane permeabilization independently of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore complex. We generated mitochondrial outer membrane-mimic liposomes to observe the direct effects of HBx on membranes. We found that HBx induced membrane permeabilization, and the region comprising the transmembrane domain and the mitochondrial targeting sequence was sufficient for this process. Membrane permeabilization was inhibited by non-selective channel blockers or by N-(n-nonyl)deoxynojirimycin (NN-DNJ), a viroporin inhibitor. Moreover, NN-DNJ inhibited HBx-induced mitochondrial depolarization in Huh-7 cells. Based on the results of the present study, we can postulate that the HBx protein itself is sufficient to induce mitochondrial membrane permeabilization. Our finding provides important information for a strategy of HBx targeting during HBV treatment. This article is protected by copyright. All rights reserved.
